body:
EDIT

This bug reported here could not be the cause of this bug, since `duplicate()` works fine when the var is not strongly typed. But it's likely related: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/74918

> All you need to do is run the code above. There is no need to provide an entire project.

We can't run that code, as it depends on class definitions which are specific to your project and not provided here.

We'd also appreciate bug reports written without insinuations that Godot contributors don't look at reported issues, or essays about the meaning of bug reporting terminology. Please stay to the fact of what you perceive to be a bug, with relevant details for contributors to confirm or challenge that assumption.

Godot has 5k issues. That is a lot of documented problems.

It is obvious that you guys could not possibly address all of them. So why are you being defensive about this? You can fault me for pointing out flaws, but this is such an obvious and openly public flaw that it's frankly a bit crazy to get defensive about it. We can all see that there are 5k issues -- that is on the high end. 

This is a red flag to say the least, as it means that people who open new issues likely will get ignored or brushed under the rug, as you currently just did to me.

How many issues Godot has is completely irrelevant to your report (for the record, it's 11,000 open issues, for 44,000 closed, so 20% of issues that haven't been resolved yet). Your issue is not being ignored as you have the project maintainer replying - and it's not being brushed under the rug, I'm just asking you to follow our guidelines to make an actual actionable bug report, instead of just throwing a small bit of code that can't compile.

Other issues like this which aren't actionable do add to the backlog indeed. We do our best to consider all issues and fix the ones which we can confirm, but a lot of the open issues are unconfirmed and might not be relevant anymore, or might have been user errors. Re-triaging those is a continuous effort and takes time, hence the somewhat high issue count - which isn't at all on the high end for a project of this size.

Here for example it's likely that both this and #102904 might be duplicated of #74918 as you identified, but there's not enough information provided to check this properly. So yeah, from 1 known and worked on issue, we now have 3 reports. You can see how that can add up.

Your issue is not being ignored as you have the project maintainer replying - and it's not being brushed under the rug, I'm just asking you to follow our guidelines to make an actual actionable bug report, instead of just throwing a small bit of code that can't compile.

Re-triaging those is a continuous effort and takes time, hence the somewhat high issue count - which isn't at all on the high end for a project of this size.

So yeah, from 1 known and worked on issue, we now have 3 reports. You can see how that can add up.

44,000 closed issues?! Wow! Do you truly believe it's possible for a small team of open source contributors to tackle 44,000 issues? I said that 5k issues is a red flag. But this is a REALLY REALLY REALLY big red flag. Obviously, the only reasonable conclusion given the scale of the Godot team is that the majority of those 44,000 issues were closed prematurely before being resolved. But to think that 44,000 issues were even opened to begin with is mind boggling.

The godot community is a cult. This engine has an ENOURMOUS amount of issues, but it gets a free pass because of it's open source wholesomeness.

Alright, I think it's time for a time out. Being rude is one thing but starting to needlessly attack the character of the project and it's contributors is another. 

Your behaviour is totally uncalled for. We appreciate your effort to help the project by making bug reports, but we can't tolerate this level of negative attitude. 

Take the weekend to cool off and then decide if you want to participate in the community or not.

Hi! As a newbie contributor, I appreciate how y'all are handling this interaction. I've been a maintainer in other large open source spaces before, I know what it can be like.

Anyway. I went and reproduced this. Here's a more minimal, copy-pasteable example:

```GDScript
extends Node

var template: Thing = Thing.new("placeholder")
var works_as_expected = [template.duplicate(true)]
var is_always_empty: Array[Thing] = [template.duplicate(true)]

func _ready():
	print(works_as_expected)
	print(is_always_empty) # prints []

class Thing extends Resource:
	var name: String
	func _init(p_name: String):
		name = p_name
```

The description is misleading. Typing an array with an initial value only causes a problem if the value in it is made with `Resource.duplicate()`. I also noticed that it only happens if the type is a custom Resource, with at least one property. So, highly likely duplicate of 74918 I'd guess.

But hey, I wouldn't have seen that issue if it wasn't for this, so now I get to go look at that one :)

Edit: That issue doesn't mention much about types, so the array typing could possibly be a separate issue, or in conjunction somehow with the other issue. We should see if the proposed fix #100673 fixes this issue.

> The godot community is a cult. This engine has an ENOURMOUS amount of issues, but it gets a free pass because of it's open source wholesomeness.

Whether that is the case or not is neither here nor there, personally I don't care one way or the other. Godot is a tool, nothing more. Something that more people, both in favor of the cult narrative as well as those against it would do well to remember.

However, what I will say though... _GitHub_ is ***not*** the place to discuss such issues. _GitHub_ is about code, about software, about technical issues with software and about bug fixing or solving such issues. It is not a therapist's sofa, it is not a bar, it is not a soapbox. Do not treat it as such. You are entitled to your views, whatever they may be. It's a free world. Just do it in a more appropriate setting. Thank you very much.
Let's move back to on topic discussion and assess the bug clarified and reproduced by @suddjian.

As of v4.7.stable.flathub [5b4e0cb0f] the MRP provided by suddjian gives the following output:

```
Godot Engine v4.7.stable.flathub.5b4e0cb0f - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.4.354 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33)

[():<Resource#-9223371999609354737>]
[<null>]
```

It also gives the following errors at runtime:

```
E 0:00:01:215   main.gd:4 @ @implicit_new(): Error constructing a GDScriptInstance: 'Resource::_init': Method expected 1 argument(s), but called with 0
E 0:00:01:215   main.gd:5 @ @implicit_new(): Error constructing a GDScriptInstance: 'Resource::_init': Method expected 1 argument(s), but called with 0
E 0:00:01:215   main.gd:5 @ @implicit_new(): Attempted to set an object into a TypedArray, that does not inherit from 'GDScript'.
E 0:00:01:215   main.gd:5 @ @implicit_new(): Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "set")" is true.
```

From those errors it's clear what's going on. The `duplicate` call can't construct the script instance, and falls back to using the partially constructed `Resource`. For the untyped array that isn't an issue because it can contain a resource. The typed array can't and is using `null` instead.

[Resource::duplicate docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-method-duplicate)

> For custom resources, this method will fail if [Object._init()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_object.html#class-object-private-method-init) has been defined with required parameters.

So by now this seems to be boiling down to a user issue that is resulting in appropriate errors. Closing.
